# Music Player 0.4.7-fork.2

This fork prerelease hardens managed Emby playback. It fixes Web playback state,
adds safe stream diagnostics, and automatically recovers from bounded transient
source failures without synchronizing Emby progress.

## Changes

- Play/Pause follows confirmed server playback. Pending commands are bounded and
  deduplicated, and command failures appear in the player bar.
- Managed playback reports resolution, startup and safe HTTP/network/decoder
  failures. Pause can cancel a stalled startup; Play retries using the retained
  queue occurrence, audio selection and playback checkpoint.
- Native Emby resolution, transport and uncertain decoder failures receive up
  to two automatic fresh-resolution retries. Every attempt preserves the queue
  occurrence, pinned audio choice, capabilities and delivered-output offset.
  Pause, Stop and Next cancel the pending timer or in-flight resolution;
  duplicate Play does not bypass it.
- Automatic recovery exhaustion keeps the same failed entry and exposes a safe
  reason for explicit Play. It does not skip to the next queue entry. Explicit
  Emby API authentication refusal and local invalid-handle/unsupported-resume
  failures remain terminal for automatic recovery.
- An Emby playback response with no selectable audio — observed on STRM items
  whose upstream target currently resolves to nothing — is reported as a
  distinct "no playable audio" condition without assuming a permanent cause.
  It receives the same bounded fresh-resolution retries. Exhaustion retains
  the last failure reason, and an explicit Play re-resolves the entry from
  the saved checkpoint.
- Subscription events refresh managed playback status when background browser
  polling is suspended.
- Settings reads and audio settings writes honor
  `MUSIC_PLAYER_APPLICATION_DIRECTORY`, so an isolated instance uses its own
  settings. Changing this directory does not migrate existing data.
- Added a local synthetic Emby server, a real Rust playback/API instance and an
  OpenCLI browser acceptance script. See `scripts/fixtures/README.md`.

## Validation

The source revision for this replacement build passed Linux amd64/arm64
distribution checks, Rust tests, Clippy, and Web UI tests/build in GitHub
Actions. The release workflows build and validate the versioned artifacts before
publication.

Local regression coverage passed: 13 native playback queue tests, 26 Emby
provider tests, 3 `sourcePlayback` GraphQL tests, 7 player-bar frontend tests and
a TypeScript check. Browser acceptance of the earlier failure-injection flows
observed real UI mutations and nonzero decoded PCM:

- Pause beyond the synthetic link's lifetime, then resume with a new session at
  the saved offset (3,680 ms in the recorded run).
- HTTP 403 failure followed by an explicit successful retry.
- Cancellation and retry of stalled startup.
- Automatic advancement from the first queue entry to the second, then stop.

Resume resolves fresh Emby playback information and uses the player's own
delivered-output checkpoint. No Emby progress synchronization is introduced.
Emby remains responsible for resolving the STRM target. The local fixture does
not establish compatibility with a real Emby/STRM upstream or production
Snapcast output. Automatic recovery is bounded; it does not claim that every
HTTP, format, audio-track or upstream outage is temporary.

## Downloads and Docker

Release workflows attach native CLI/desktop downloads and adjacent SHA-256
checksums as each platform completes. The Linux CLI workflow publishes DEB/RPM
packages, archives, validation evidence and this multi-platform image:

```sh
docker pull ghcr.io/killbus/music-player:0.4.7-fork.2
```

The image supports `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`. There is no `latest` alias.
Use the version tag or published digest, persist `/data`, and keep your existing
audio output configuration. See `dist/README.md` for package and container setup.

DEB/RPM metadata uses `0.4.7~fork.2`; application and image versions use
`0.4.7-fork.2`. The previous release remains available as `0.4.7-fork.1`.
Preserve persistent settings and library/database data when switching versions;
selecting an older binary does not roll back data.
